entities.summary: Elman Ali Ahmed was a Somali entrepreneur and social activist who played a pivotal role in promoting education and economic empowerment for women in East Africa. Born in the 1950s, Ahmed co-founded the Somali Women's Development and Business Association (SWDBA) in 1985, which aimed to provide training and support for women entrepreneurs in Somalia. Through SWDBA, Ahmed helped establish a network of female-run businesses, generating employment and income for thousands of Somali women. His efforts also contributed to the development of Somalia's first women's bank, the Somali Women's Bank, which provided microfinance loans to women and helped stimulate economic growth. Ahmed's legacy extends beyond Somalia, as his work inspired a new generation of women's empowerment initiatives across East Africa. He died on March 9, 1996, leaving behind a lasting impact on the lives of countless Somali women and their families. Ahmed's story is a testament to the power of grassroots activism and the importance of supporting women's economic development. As a Somali entrepreneur and social activist, Elman Ali Ahmed remains an important figure in the history of East African women's empowerment.
